Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 60, verse 1:

Surat al-Mumtahana is Medinan [[Ibn al-Duraymi, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: Surat al-Mumtahana was revealed in Medina. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated the same from Ibn al-Zubayr. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/124.]] In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

* *

﴿O you who believe, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ to the end of the verse.

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us: Qutayba ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us from ʿAmr ibn Dinar: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed me that he heard ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Rafiʿ say: I heard ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me, al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad, and said: "Set out until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman traveller with a letter; take it from her." He said: So we set off, our horses galloping with us, until we reached the garden, and there we found the woman traveller. We said: "Bring out the letter." She said: "I have no letter with me." We said: "Either you bring out the letter or we will strip off your clothes." He said: So she took it out from her braid, and we brought it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). In it was (a letter) from Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a to some people of the polytheists in Mecca, informing them of some of the affairs of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "O Hatib, what is this?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, do not hasten to judge me. I was a man attached to Quraysh (he means I was an ally and not one of their own kin), and those of the Emigrants who are with you have relatives there who protect their families and property. I wanted, since I had no lineage among them, to make a favour with them so that they would protect my relatives. I did not do it out of apostasy from my religion, nor out of contentment with disbelief after Islam." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed he has told you the truth." ʿUmar said: "O Messenger of Allah, let me strike the neck of this hypocrite." He said: "He has witnessed Badr. What do you know? Perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you." So Allah the Exalted revealed this surah: "O you who believe, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, showing them affection," to His words "the right way." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Jihad, chapter on the spy: 6/143, and Muslim in the Virtues of the Companions, chapter on the virtues of the people of Badr and the story of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a, no. (2494): 4/1941-1942.]]

The commentators said: The verse was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a, as came in the hadith. The reason was that Sara, a freedwoman of Abu ʿAmr ibn Sayfi ibn Hashim ibn ʿAbd Manaf, came to Medina from Mecca while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was preparing for the conquest of Mecca. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Have you come as a Muslim?" She said: "No." He said: "Have you come as an emigrant?" She said: "No." He said: "Then what brought you?" She said: "You are the origin, the kin and the clients, and my clients have perished, and I have fallen into severe need, so I came to you so that you might give me, clothe me and carry me." He said to her: "And where are you from the young men of Mecca?" She was a singing-girl and a mourner. She said: "I have not been asked for anything since the Battle of Badr." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) urged the sons of ʿAbd al-Muttalib and the sons of al-Muttalib, and they gave her provisions, clothed her and carried her. Then Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a, an ally of the Banu Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzza, came to her, wrote with her a letter to the people of Mecca, and gave her ten dinars and a striped cloak, on condition that she deliver the letter to the people of Mecca. In the letter he wrote: "From Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a to the people of Mecca: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intends you, so take your precaution."

Sara set out, and Gabriel descended and informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of what had been done. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent ʿAli, ʿAmmar, al-Zubayr, Talha, al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad and Abu Marthad as mounted horsemen, and said to them: "Set out until you reach 'Rawdat Khakh', for there is a woman traveller with a letter from Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a to the polytheists. Take from her, and let her go on her way; but if she does not hand it over to you, then strike her neck."

He said: So they set out until they overtook her at that very place which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had mentioned. They said to her: "Where is the letter?" She swore by Allah that she had no letter with her. They searched her and went through her belongings, but found no letter with her, and they were about to return. ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "By Allah, we have not lied, nor has the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lied," and he drew his sword and said: "Bring out the letter, or I will strip you bare and strike your neck." When she saw the earnestness, she took it out from her braid, for she had hidden it in her hair. So they let her go on her way and did not interfere with her or with what she had. They returned with the letter to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who sent for Hatib. He came, and he said: "Do you recognise this letter?" He said: "Yes." He said: "What moved you to do what you did?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I have not disbelieved since I embraced Islam, nor have I deceived you since I gave you counsel, nor have I loved them since I parted from them. But there was no one among the Emigrants except that he had someone in Mecca who protects his kin, and I was a stranger among them, and my family was among them. I feared for my family, so I wished to make a favour with them. I knew that Allah would send down His might upon them, and that my letter would not avail them anything." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted his word and excused him.

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab stood up and said: "Let me, O Messenger of Allah, strike the neck of this hypocrite." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What do you know, O ʿUmar? Perhaps Allah has looked upon the people of Badr and said to them: Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning the matter of Hatib: "O you who believe, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies."

﴿showing them affection﴾ It is said: the meaning is "bi-al-mawaddah," and the "ba'" is extra, as in His words: "and whoever intends therein a deviation with injustice" [al-Hajj: 25]. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is that you convey to them the news and secrets of the Prophet (ﷺ) through the affection that is between you and them. ﴿And they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth﴾ — the "waw" is for the circumstantial clause, meaning: while they have disbelieved. ﴿Meaning the Qur'an.﴾ ﴿They expel the Messenger and you﴾ from Mecca ﴿because you believe in Allah, your Lord.﴾ That is, because you have believed; as if He said: they do that because of your faith. ﴿If you have gone out﴾ — this is a conditional clause whose answer is placed before it, namely His words: "do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, showing them affection, while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth, if you have gone out" ﴿striving in My way and seeking My pleasure.﴾ ﴿You confide to them with affection﴾. Muqatil said: with counsel. ﴿And I am most knowing of what you conceal﴾ of affection for the disbelievers ﴿and what you declare﴾, what you show with your tongues. ﴿And whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the right way﴾ — he has erred from the path of guidance.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 60, verse 2:

﴿If they overcome you﴾ (yathqafuukum): they gain the upper hand over you and see you, ﴿they will be your enemies and will stretch out their hands to you﴾ with beating and killing, ﴿and their tongues with evil﴾ with abuse, ﴿and they wish that you would disbelieve﴾ as they disbelieved. He says: do not give them sincere counsel, for they do not give you sincere counsel and they do not show you affection.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 60, verse 3–5:

﴿Your relatives and your children will never benefit you﴾. Its meaning: your kin, your relatives, and your children who are in Makkah shall not urge you nor compel you toward betraying the Messenger (ﷺ) and the believers, and toward abandoning giving them sincere counsel and toward allying with their enemies. So ﴿your relatives will never benefit you﴾ ﴿nor your children﴾, those for whose sake you disobeyed Allah, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection He will separate between you﴾, so He will admit the people of His obedience to Paradise and the people of His disobedience to the Fire. ʿĀṣim and Yaʿqūb read ﴿yafṣilu﴾ with a fatḥah on the yā' and a kasrah on the ṣād, lightened (mukhaffafan). Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī read it with a ḍammah on the yā' and a kasrah on the ṣād, emphasized (mushaddadan). [Ibn ʿĀmir read it with a ḍammah on the yā' and a fatḥah on the ṣād, emphasized] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "a".]] The others read it with a ḍammah on the yā' and a fatḥah on the ṣād, lightened.

﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾. ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example﴾, a model ﴿in Ibrahim and those with him﴾ from among the people of faith, ﴿when they said to their people﴾ from among the polytheists, ﴿Indeed, we are free of you﴾, the plural of barī', ﴿and of what you worship other than Allah. We have disbelieved in you﴾, we denied and rejected your religion, ﴿and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone﴾. He commands Ḥāṭib and the believers to take Ibrahim (peace be upon him) as a model, and those with him among the believers, in disavowing the polytheists. ﴿Except for the saying of Ibrahim to his father: I will surely ask forgiveness for you﴾. That is: you have an excellent example in Ibrahim and his affairs, except in his seeking forgiveness for his polytheist father, for Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had said to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you," then he disavowed him, as we mentioned in Surah al-Tawbah [[See above: 4/101.]]. ﴿And I have no power for you against Allah in anything﴾. Ibrahim says to his father: I cannot avail you nor ward off from you the punishment of Allah if you disobey Him and associate others with Him. ﴿Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned in repentance, and to You is the final return﴾. Ibrahim and those with him among the believers say this.

﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us. Our Lord, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ (5)

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 60, verses 6–8:**

﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve﴾. Al-Zajjaj (a grammarian and exegete) said: "Do not let them prevail over us, lest they think that they are upon the truth and so be tested (by their error)." Mujahid said: "Do not punish us at their hands, nor with a punishment from You, lest they say: 'If these were upon the truth, this would not have befallen them.'" [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 28/64. See also al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/225 and Ibn Kathir: 4/394.]] ﴿And forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, You are the Almighty, the Wise﴾.

﴿There is certainly for you in them﴾, that is, in Ibrahim and those with him, ﴿an excellent example for whoever hopes for Allah and the Last Day﴾. This is a substitution (badal) for His words "for you" and an explanation that this excellent example is for whoever fears Allah and fears the punishment of the Hereafter. ﴿And whoever turns away﴾ means turns away from faith and takes the disbelievers as allies. ﴿Then indeed Allah is the Free of need﴾ from His creation, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾, with regard to His allies and the people of His obedience.

Muqatil said: When Allah commanded the believers to be hostile toward the disbelievers, the believers became hostile to their relatives among the polytheists, and they openly showed them enmity and disassociation. Allah knew the intensity of the believers' grief over this, so Allah revealed [[Mentioned by Ibn Kathir: 4/349–350. See Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. (488).]] ﴿It may be that Allah will place affection between you and those among them whom you have been hostile to﴾, that is, among the disbelievers of Makkah. ﴿Affection.﴾ So Allah did that, and many of them embraced Islam, and they became allies and brothers to them, mixed with them and intermarried with them. ﴿And Allah is All-Powerful, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Then Allah, exalted is He, permitted the kindness of those who had not been hostile to the believers and had not fought them. He said: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over the religion and do not expel you from your homes, from being righteous to them and acting justly toward them﴾. ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over the religion and do not expel you from your homes, from being righteous to them.﴾ That is, Allah does not forbid you from showing kindness to those who have not fought you. ﴿And act justly toward them﴾ means deal with them equitably, with goodness and kindness. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.﴾

Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed concerning Khuza'ah, who had made a treaty with the Prophet (ﷺ) that they would not fight him and would not assist anyone against him, so Allah permitted kindness toward them.

Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr said: It was revealed concerning Asma' bint Abi Bakr. Her mother, Qutaylah bint Abd al-Uzza, came to her in Madinah with gifts: lizards, dried curd, and clarified butter, while she was a polytheist. Asma' said: "I will not accept a gift from you, and do not enter my house until I seek permission from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." She asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah revealed this verse. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded her to bring her into her home, accept her gift, honor her, and treat her well. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 28/66; Ahmad: 4/4; al-Hakim: 2/485–486, who graded it sahih and was agreed with by al-Dhahabi. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/123: "Narrated by Ahmad and al-Bazzar, and in its chain is Mus'ab ibn Thabit, whom Ibn Hibban declared trustworthy, but many have declared weak, and the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih."]]

Al-Malihi informed us: Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) narrated to us, Qutaybah narrated to us, Hatim narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "My mother came to me while she was a polytheist, during the time of the Quraysh treaty, when they had made a covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) along with their truce. I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for a ruling and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, my mother has come to me and she desires (my kindness). Should I maintain ties with her?' He said: 'Maintain ties with her.'" [[Recorded by al-Bukhari in Hibah, chapter on gifts to polytheists: 5/233; and Muslim in Zakah, chapter on the virtue of spending and giving charity to near relatives, spouse, children, and parents even if they are polytheists, no. (1003): 2/696.]]

It is related from Ibn Uyaynah who said: Allah revealed concerning her: "Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over the religion." Then He mentioned those whom He forbade them from maintaining ties with, saying: ﴿Allah only forbids you from those who fight you over the religion, expel you from your homes, and help others in your expulsion﴾.

This is a substitution (badal) for His words "for you" and an explanation that this excellent example is for whoever fears Allah and fears the punishment of the Hereafter. ﴿And whoever turns away﴾ means turns away from faith and takes the disbelievers as allies. ﴿Then indeed Allah is the Free of need﴾ from His creation, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾, with regard to His allies and the people of His obedience.

Muqatil said: When Allah commanded the believers to be hostile toward the disbelievers, the believers became hostile to their relatives among the polytheists, and they openly showed them enmity and disassociation. Allah knew the intensity of the believers' grief over this, so Allah revealed [[Mentioned by Ibn Kathir: 4/349–350. See Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. (488).]] ﴿It may be that Allah will place affection between you and those among them whom you have been hostile to﴾, that is, among the disbelievers of Makkah. ﴿Affection.﴾ So Allah did that, and many of them embraced Islam, and they became allies and brothers to them, mixed with them and intermarried with them. ﴿And Allah is All-Powerful, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Then Allah, exalted is He, permitted the kindness of those who had not been hostile to the believers and had not fought them. He said: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over the religion and do not expel you from your homes, from being righteous to them and acting justly toward them﴾. ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over the religion and do not expel you from your homes, from being righteous to them.﴾ That is, Allah does not forbid you from showing kindness to those who have not fought you. ﴿And act justly toward them﴾ means deal with them equitably, with goodness and kindness. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.﴾

Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed concerning Khuza'ah, who had made a treaty with the Prophet (ﷺ) that they would not fight him and would not assist anyone against him, so Allah permitted kindness toward them.

Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr said: It was revealed concerning Asma' bint Abi Bakr. Her mother, Qutaylah bint Abd al-Uzza, came to her in Madinah with gifts: lizards, dried curd, and clarified butter, while she was a polytheist. Asma' said: "I will not accept a gift from you, and do not enter my house until I seek permission from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." She asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah revealed this verse. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded her to bring her into her home, accept her gift, honor her, and treat her well. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 28/66; Ahmad: 4/4; al-Hakim: 2/485–486, who graded it sahih and was agreed with by al-Dhahabi. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/123: "Narrated by Ahmad and al-Bazzar, and in its chain is Mus'ab ibn Thabit, whom Ibn Hibban declared trustworthy, but many have declared weak, and the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih."]]

Al-Malihi informed us: Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) narrated to us, Qutaybah narrated to us, Hatim narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "My mother came to me while she was a polytheist, during the time of the Quraysh treaty, when they had made a covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) along with their truce. I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for a ruling and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, my mother has come to me and she desires (my kindness). Should I maintain ties with her?' He said: 'Maintain ties with her.'" [[Recorded by al-Bukhari in Hibah, chapter on gifts to polytheists: 5/233; and Muslim in Zakah, chapter on the virtue of spending and giving charity to near relatives, spouse, children, and parents even if they are polytheists, no. (1003): 2/696.]]

It is related from Ibn Uyaynah who said: Allah revealed concerning her: "Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over the religion." Then He mentioned those whom He forbade them from maintaining ties with, saying: ﴿Allah only forbids you from those who fight you over the religion, expel you from your homes, and help others in your expulsion﴾.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants, then test them...﴾ the verse.

Abdul-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari] narrated to us, Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Marwan and al-Miswar ibn Makhramah relate from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they said: When Suhayl ibn Amr wrote the treaty that day, among the conditions Suhayl ibn Amr stipulated to the Prophet (ﷺ) was: "No one from us will come to you, even if he is upon your religion, except that you return him to us, and you leave him between us and him." The believers disliked this, but Suhayl refused anything other than this. So the Prophet (ﷺ) agreed to it in writing. That day the Prophet (ﷺ) returned Abu Jandal to his father Suhayl ibn Amr, and no man came to him except that he returned him during that period, even if he was a Muslim. Believing women then came as emigrants, and Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt was among those who went out to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that day as an emigrant, and she was a young unmarried woman. Her family came asking the Prophet (ﷺ) to return her to them, but he did not return her to them, because of what Allah revealed concerning them: "When believing women come to you as emigrants, then test them; Allah knows best their faith," up to "nor are they lawful for them."

Urwah said: Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, informed me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to test them with this verse: "O Prophet, when believing women come to you..." up to his saying: "Forgiving, Merciful."

Urwah said: Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: Whoever of them acknowledged this condition, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would say to her: "I have accepted your pledge," by mere speech. By Allah, his hand never touched the hand of any woman in the pledge; he only pledged them with his words. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Shurut, chapter on what is permissible of conditions in Islam, rules and pledges: 5/213, and in fuller form in the chapter on conditions in jihad: 5/329-332; Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on how the pledge of women is taken (1866): 3/1489; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/157-158.]]

Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out as a pilgrim for 'Umrah, and when he reached al-Hudaybiyah, the polytheists of Makkah made a treaty with him that whoever came to him from the people of Makkah, he would return to them, and whoever went from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the people of Makkah, they would not return to him. They wrote this down in a document and sealed it. Then Subay'ah bint al-Harith al-Aslamiyyah came as a Muslim woman after the completion of the document. Her husband, Musafir of Banu Makhzum, (and Muqatil said he was Sayfi ibn al-Rahib), came seeking her. He was a disbeliever, and he said: "O Muhammad, return my wife to me, for you have stipulated that you would return to us whoever comes to you from us." This was the ink of the document, not yet dry. So Allah, Exalted and Majestic, revealed: "O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants," from the abode of disbelief to the abode of Islam, ﴿then test them﴾.

Ibn Abbas said: Their test was that they be made to swear that they did not go out out of hatred for their husbands, nor out of love for a man among the Muslims, nor out of desire to move from one land to another, nor because of some innovation they had introduced, nor to seek worldly gain; they only went out out of desire for Islam and love for Allah and His Messenger.

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then made them swear to this, and they swore, and he did not return them. He gave their husbands their mahr (bridal gift) and what they had spent on them. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, married her. [[See: Ibn Kathir 4/351; al-Durr al-Manthur 8/137; al-Qurtubi 18/62.]] Umar used to return the men who came to him, and after testing he would detain the women who came to him, and he would give their husbands their mahr.

﴿Allah knows best their faith﴾ [meaning: this testing is for you, and Allah knows best about them]. ﴿If you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them.﴾ It is not permissible for a believing woman to be married to a disbeliever. ﴿And give them﴾ meaning their disbelieving husbands ﴿what they have spent﴾ on them, meaning the mahr they paid to them. ﴿And there is no blame on you if you marry them when you have given them their wages﴾, meaning their mahr. Allah permitted the Muslims to marry them, even if they had husbands in the abode of disbelief, because Islam had separated them from their disbelieving husbands. ﴿And do not hold on to disbelieving women in marriage﴾ [Abu Amr and Ya'qub read it with the doubled letter, and the others with the single letter, from al-Imsak (holding)]. ﴿Ismah of the disbelievers﴾. "Al-Isam" is the plural of "al-'Ismah," which is that by which one is protected, through marriage bond and kinship. "Al-Kawafir" is the plural of "al-Kafirah."

Allah forbade the believers from remaining in marriage with polytheist women. He says: whoever had a disbelieving wife in Makkah, he should not hold on to her, for the bond of marriage between them has been severed.

Al-Zuhri said: When this verse was revealed, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, divorced two wives he had in Makkah who were polytheists: Qurayba bint Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah, and then Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married her after him, while they were still upon their polytheism in Makkah. The other was Umm Kulthum bint Amr ibn Jarwal al-Khuza'iyyah, the mother of his son Abdullah ibn Umar, and Abu Jahm ibn Hudhayfah ibn Ghanim married her, while they were still upon their polytheism. Arwa bint Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib was married to Talhah ibn Ubaydullah; Talhah emigrated while she was in Makkah upon the religion of her people, so Islam separated them. Then Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-As ibn Umayyah married her in Islam. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/72. See also Ibn Kathir 4/352.]]

Al-Sha'bi said: Zaynab, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was the wife of Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi'. She embraced Islam and joined the Prophet (ﷺ), while Abu al-As remained in Makkah as a polytheist. Then he came to Madinah and embraced Islam, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned her to him. [[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 8/136 to Abd ibn Humayd. Also mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir: 4/352. See what al-Hafiz Ibn Abd al-Barr wrote in al-Tamhid: 12/19-35, and see Irwa' al-Ghalil: 6/339-341.]]

﴿And ask﴾, O believers, ﴿for what you have spent﴾, meaning: if a woman from among you apostatizes and joins the polytheists, then ask for the mahr you spent, if they prevent her from being married to whoever marries her among them. ﴿And let them ask﴾, meaning the polytheists whose wives joined you, ﴿for what they spent﴾ as mahr, from whoever among you marries her. ﴿That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾

Al-Zuhri said: Had it not been for the truce and the covenant that existed between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Quraysh on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, he would have held on to the women and not returned the bridal payment; and he used to do likewise with the Muslim women who came to him before the covenant. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/74. al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 8/136-137 added its attribution to Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, and Ibn al-Mundhir.]] When this verse was revealed, the believers acknowledged the judgment of Allah, Exalted and Majestic, and paid what they were commanded to pay of the polytheists' expenses on their wives. But the polytheists refused to acknowledge Allah's judgment regarding what they were commanded to pay of the Muslims' expenses [on their wives], [[Omitted in "A".]] so Allah, Exalted and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And if you lose [any wife] to the disbelievers...﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 60, verse 11:

﴿And if any of your wives go over to the disbelievers﴾, O believers, ﴿and you then have a turn﴾. The commentators (*mufassirun*) said: its meaning is "you gained spoils," that is, you fought and obtained from the disbelievers an *'uqba*, which is booty (*ghanima*). It was also said: you prevailed, and the final outcome (*'aqiba*) was in your favour. It was also said: you struck them in battle with a punishment until you gained spoils. Ḥumayd al-A'raj recited "*fa-'aqqabtum*" with the doubled *qaf*. Al-Zuhri recited "*fa-'aqabtum*" without the *alif* and with the *qaf* unstressed. Mujahid recited "*fa-a'qabtum*," meaning you treated them as they had treated you. All of these are dialectal variants with one meaning. It is said: *'aqaba*, *'aqqaba*, *'aqiba*, *a'qaba*, *ta'aqqaba*, *ta'aqaba* and *i'taqaba* all mean "he gained spoils." It was also said that *al-ta'qib* means one raid after another.

﴿Then give to those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent﴾ on them from the spoils that have come into your hands from the wealth of the disbelievers. It was also said: ﴿you then have a turn﴾ against the apostate woman by putting her to death.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Six women from the wives of the believers and the emigrants (*muhajirun*) went over to the polytheists: Umm al-Hakam bint Abi Sufyan, who had been married to 'Iyad ibn Shaddad al-Fihri; Fatimah bint Abi Umayya ibn al-Mughira, sister of Umm Salama, who had been married to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and when 'Umar wanted to emigrate she refused and apostatised; Barwa' bint 'Uqba, who had been married to Shammas ibn 'Uthman; 'Izza bint 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Nadla, whose husband was 'Amr ibn 'Abd Wudd; Hind bint Abi Jahl ibn Hisham, who had been married to Hisham ibn al-'As ibn Wa'il; and Umm Kulthum bint Jarwal, who had been married to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. All of them turned back from Islam, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave their husbands the bridal gifts (*mahr*) of their wives from the spoils. [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/257.]]

﴿And fear Allah, in whom you are believers﴾. Scholars have differed over whether the returning of the *mahr* to the husbands of women who embraced Islam was obligatory or recommended (*mandub*).

The root of this disagreement is whether the treaty (*sulh*) had been concluded on the return of the women. There are two opinions. The first is that it was concluded on the return of both men and women, based on what we have related: "No one will come to you from us, even if he is upon your religion, except that you return him to us." Then the ruling concerning the return of women was abrogated (*mansukh*) by the words of Allah, "So do not return them to the disbelievers." According to this view, returning the *mahr* was obligatory.

The second opinion is that the treaty was not concluded on the return of women, because it is related from 'Ali that the treaty said: "No man will come to you from us, even if he is upon your religion, except that you return him to us." The reasoning is that a man is not feared to be subjected to temptation upon return in the way a woman is feared to be harmed by a polytheist's contact with her. Moreover, a woman cannot be trusted against apostasy if she is threatened and coerced into it, because of the weakness of her heart and her lesser ability to find a way out by uttering a word of disbelief while using equivocation (*tawriya*) and concealing faith. Such a risk is not feared for a man, given his strength and his ability to practise dissimulation (*taqiyya*). According to this view, returning the *mahr* was recommended.

They differed over whether it is still obligatory today to act upon this ruling regarding the return of property when it is stipulated in a treaty with the disbelievers. Some people said it is not obligatory, claiming that the verse is abrogated; this is the view of 'Ata', Mujahid and Qatada. Others said it is not abrogated, and what they spent is to be returned to them.

**The Qur'anic exegete said:** His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you...﴾ the verse. This was on the day of the Conquest of Makkah, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had finished taking the pledge of allegiance from the men. He was on al-Safa, and Umar ibn al-Khattab was below him, taking the pledge from the women by the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and conveying it to them on his behalf. Hind bint Utbah, the wife of Abu Sufyan, was among the women, veiled and disguised, fearing that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would recognize her. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I take your pledge that you will not associate anything with Allah." Hind raised her head and said: "By Allah, you are requiring of us a matter which we have not seen you require of the men." The men had pledged that day only to Islam and to jihad. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "And that they will not steal." Hind said: "Abu Sufyan is a stingy man, and I have taken some of his property, certain trifles, and I do not know whether that is lawful for me or not." Abu Sufyan said: "Whatever you have taken in the past and what remains is lawful for you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed and recognized her, and said to her: "Are you indeed Hind bint Utbah?" She said: "Yes. So pardon what has passed; may Allah pardon you." He said: "And that they will not commit adultery." Hind said: "Does a free woman commit adultery?" He said: "And that they will not kill their children." Hind said: "We raised them when they were small, and you killed them when they were grown; so you and they know best." Her son Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan had been killed on the day of Badr. Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, laughed until he fell backwards, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) smiled. He said: "And that they will not bring a slander which they have invented between their hands and their feet," which means that a woman attributes to her husband a child that is not his. Hind said: "By Allah, slander is indeed ugly, and you only command us to what is right and to noble character." He said: "And that they will not disobey you in what is reasonable." Hind said: "We have not sat in this gathering of ours while in our hearts there is any intention to disobey you in anything." Then the women acknowledged what had been required of them. [[Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir: 4/354-355, then said: "This is a strange report, and some of it contains objectionable content, and Allah knows best." See also al-Bahr al-Muhit 8/258.]]

His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿and that they will not kill their children﴾ means the burying of daughters alive, which the people of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic period of ignorance) used to do.

His statement: ﴿nor bring a slander which they have invented between their hands and their feet﴾ does not mean forbidding them from fornication, because the prohibition of fornication has already been mentioned. Rather, it means that a woman picks up a newborn and says to her husband: "This is my child from you," and this is the invented slander "between their hands and their feet," because when the mother gives birth, the child falls between her hands and feet.

His statement: ﴿nor disobey you in what is reasonable﴾ means in every matter that is in accordance with the obedience of Allah. Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani said: "In every matter in which there is their right guidance." Mujahid said: "A woman must not be alone with men." Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Kalbi and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: it is the prohibition of wailing, calling for destruction, tearing clothes, shaving or plucking the hair, and scratching the face. A woman must not speak to men except one who is a mahram (a relative whom she may never marry), must not be alone with a man who is not a mahram, and must not travel except with a mahram.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il said to us, Abu Ma'mar said to us, Abd al-Warith said to us, Ayyub said to us, from Hafsah bint Sirin, from Umm Atiyyah, who said: "We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he recited to us: 'that they will not associate anything with Allah,' and he forbade us from wailing. Then a woman withdrew her hand and said: 'So-and-so made me happy, and I want to repay her.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said nothing to her. She went away, then came back, and he took her pledge." [[Reported by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir, chapter of Surat al-Mumtahanah, the chapter "(When believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you)," 8/637.]]

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us, al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Dinawari informed us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq said to us, Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said to us, Hudbah ibn Khalid said to us, Aban ibn Yazid said to us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir said to us, that Zayd told him that Abu Salam told him that Abu Malik al-Ash'ari told him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Four practices of the Jahiliyyah remain among my community, and they will not abandon them: boasting of lineage, slandering of ancestry, seeking rain through the stars, and wailing." And he said: "The wailing woman, if she does not repent before her death, will rise on the Day of Resurrection wearing a garment of tar and a coat of scabies." [[Reported by Abu Ya'la in his Musnad: 2/235; Muslim in the Funerals, chapter on the severity regarding wailing, no. (934): 2/644; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/437.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il said to us, Amr ibn Hafs said to us, my father said to us, al-A'mash informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from Abd Allah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He is not of us who strikes the cheeks, tears the collars, and calls with the calls of the Jahiliyyah." [[Reported by al-Bukhari in the Funerals, chapter: "He is not of us who strikes the cheeks": 3/166; Muslim in Faith, chapter on the prohibition of striking the cheeks, no. (103): 1/99; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/436.]]

His statement: ﴿So accept their pledge﴾ means: when they pledge allegiance to you, then accept their pledge. ﴿And ask Allah's forgiveness for them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il said to us, Mahmud related to me, Abd al-Razzaq said to us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to take the pledge of the women by speech, with this verse: "They will not associate anything with Allah." She said: "The hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never touched the hand of a woman except a woman whom he owned." [[Reported by al-Bukhari in the Judgments, chapter on the pledge of the women: 13/203; Muslim in Leadership, chapter on the manner of the women's pledge, no. (1866): 3/1489; and Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 6/7.]]

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, Makki ibn Abdan informed us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr said to us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who heard Umaymah bint Ruqayqah say: "I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) along with a group of women. He said to us: 'In what you are able and capable of.' I said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is more merciful to us than we are to ourselves.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, take our pledge.'" Sufyan said: "That is, shake our hands." He said: "I do not shake hands with women. My word to one woman is like my word to a hundred women." [[Reported by al-Tirmidhi in Siyar, chapter on what has come concerning the pledge of the women: 5/220, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith"; al-Nasa'i in Bay'ah, chapter on the pledge of the women: 7/149; Ibn Majah in Jihad, chapter on the pledge of the women, no. (2874): 2/959; Imam Ahmad: 6/357; Imam Malik in al-Muwatta': 2/982; Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 6/7; and Ibn Hibban, no. (12), page (34). See also Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah, no. (259).]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 60, verse 13:

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿O you who believe, do not take as allies a people with whom Allah is angry﴾. They are the Jews. This is because some of the poorer Muslims used to inform the Jews of the news of the Muslims, seeking thereby to ingratiate themselves with them and obtain some of their fruits. So Allah forbade them from that [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit, 8/259.]]. ﴿They have despaired﴾, meaning these Jews, ﴿of the Hereafter﴾, that there should be for them in it any reward or good, ﴿as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves﴾, i.e., as the disbelievers who have died and become in the graves have despaired of having any share or reward in the Hereafter. Mujahid said: "The disbelievers, when they entered their graves, despaired of the mercy of Allah." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "They despaired of the Hereafter as the disbelievers who died and then witnessed the Hereafter have despaired." It was also said: "As the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves returning to them."
